# HubbardShowBasis

Module: **FTI** · directory: `FTI/src/HubbardModels` · binary: `FTI/src/Programs/HubbardModels/HubbardShowBasis`

```text
HubbardShowBasis, version 0.01

Usage: HubbardShowBasis [options] 

Options:

system options:
    -p, --nbr-particles : number of particles (default value = 4)
    -x, --nbr-sites : number of flux quanta (default value = 20)
    --conserve-sz : Sz is a good quantum number
    --total-spin : twice the total spin value (default value = 0)
    --boson : use bosonic statistics instead of fermionic statistic
    --su2-spin : use bosonic statistics
    --gutzwiller : use the Gutzwiller projection
    --fixed-parity : only fix the parity of the number of particles
    --parity : parity of the number of particles when using --fixed-parity (can be 0 or 1) (default value = 0)
    --get-index : find the index of a given n-body state
    --xperiodic-boundary : use periodic boundary conditions in the x direction
    --x-periodicity : periodicity in the number of site index that implements the periodic boundary condition in the x direction (use only for 1d) (default value = 4)
    --x-momentum : momentum along the x direction (default value = 0)
    --max-xmomentum : number of momentum in the x direction (default value = 4)
    --2dperiodic-boundaries : use periodic boundary conditions in the x and y directions
    --y-momentum : set the momentum along the y direction (default value = 0)
    --max-ymomentum : number of momentum in the y direction (default value = 2)
    --szsymmetrized-basis : use the Sz <-> -Sz symmetry
    --sz-parity : select the  Sz <-> -Sz parity (can be 1 or -1) (default value = 1)
    --cluster-exclusion : restrict Hilbert space to plaquettes with at most 6 particles
    --add-index : add index of the Hilbert space vectors
    --state : name of an optional vector state whose component values can be displayed behind each corresponding n-body state
    -c, --complex-vector : vector state is complex instead of real
    --hide-component : hide state components (and thus the corresponding n-body state) whose absolute value is lower than a given error (0 if all components have to be shown (default value = 0)

output options:
    --save-disk : save output on disk
    --output-file : use this file name instead of statistics_hubbard_suN_n_nbrparticles_q_nbrfluxquanta_z_totallz.basis

misc options:
    -h, --help : display this help

global options:
    --append-cmdline : append command line to file
```
